ev.q: Influenza vaccination coverage among HCP during the 2016–17 influenza season, assessed using an opt-in Internet panel survey, was 78.6%
Among all HCP, coverage increased from 63.5% in the 2010–11 season to 75.2% in the 2013–14 season
Overall, 78.6% of survey respondents reported receiving vaccination during the 2016–17 season
Overall, 78.6% of respondents reported having received an influenza vaccination during the 2016–17 season
Vaccination coverage was lowest (45.8%) among HCP working in locations where employers did not require vaccination
coverage in hospital, ambulatory care, and LTC settings was similar in 2015–16 and 2016–17
CDC conducted an opt-in Internet panel survey of 2,438 HCP
Among all HCP, coverage increased from 63.5% in the 2010–11 season to 75.2% in the 2013–14 season

methods_quotes.q: Because the study sample was based on HCP from opt-in Internet panels rather than probability samples, statistical testing was not conducted.
An increase or decrease of at least 5 percentage points between seasonal estimates was considered a change; estimates with smaller differences were considered similar.
Responses were weighted to the distribution of the U.S. population of health care personnel by occupation
Weights were calculated based on each occupation type, by age, sex, race/ethnicity, work setting, and U.S. Census region
Vaccination coverage estimate not reliable because the sample size was <30.
